claims.text: The identity of X (Al, Si, or Mn) controls protective oxide behavior in CrFeCoNiX alloys through its effects on diffusion kinetics and oxide-phase stability.
The diffusion behavior and oxidation kinetics of X determine oxide-scale microstructure and adhesion.
Al has slower diffusion kinetics in these alloys under the stated oxidation conditions.
Si has slower diffusion kinetics in these alloys under the stated oxidation conditions.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys preferentially form a slow-growing, dense, coherent Al2O3 scale.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys preferentially form a slow-growing, dense, coherent silica-based scale.
The proposed Al2O3 or silica-based scales have low lattice mismatch with the substrate and consequently low growth stress.
Mn has higher diffusivity than Al or Si in the relevant CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys oxidize rapidly and predominantly form manganese oxides.
The manganese oxide scales are porous or loose and develop high internal stresses.
Mn-bearing oxide scales are prone to cracking and spallation.
Oxides formed on CrMnFeCoNi are non-protective and deplete the alloy of Mn.
Al-containing alloys will retain continuous, adherent, slow-growing protective scales during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Si-containing alloys will retain continuous, adherent, slow-growing protective scales during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Mn-containing alloys will develop rapidly thickening, unstable oxide layers that crack or spall and degrade oxidation resistance.
The proposed mechanism applies above 900 °C in oxidative atmospheres.
The proposed mechanism also applies in unspecified corrosive atmospheres.
The proposed mechanism applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Minor compositional variations affect oxide-growth kinetics and scale coherence.

Failure of Al- or Si-bearing alloys to form coherent, adherent, slow-growing scales, or formation of equally protective scales on Mn-bearing alloys, would falsify the proposed element-specific mechanism.
